Question: Can a Christian be sanctified and still struggle with sin?
ShortAnswer: Yes — struggling with sin is not proof that sanctification has failed; it is the normal experience of Christians in this life. Sanctification is real growth, not instant perfection, and even Paul described the ongoing fight in Romans 7.
DetailedAnswer: Romans 7 is the most honest passage in the Bible about this struggle: Paul writes, 'I do not do the good I want to do, but the evil I do not want to do — this I keep on doing' (Romans 7:19). Whether Paul is describing his pre-Christian or Christian experience, the passage captures what every believer knows: wanting to obey and still failing. John is equally blunt: 'If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves' (1 John 1:8) — and in the same breath he promises that confessed sin is forgiven (1 John 1:9). Sanctification means you are genuinely changing — new desires, new victories, new hatred of sin — but the change is progressive: Paul says, 'Not that I have already obtained all this... but I press on' (Philippians 3:12). The difference between a Christian struggling with sin and an unbeliever is not perfection but direction: the Christian grieves over sin, confesses it, and keeps fighting, while the unbeliever makes peace with it. If you are struggling, that struggle itself is evidence the Spirit is at work. Keep confessing, keep repenting, keep trusting grace — and measure growth over years, not days.
